reader.requirement: At COBOL-85 a user-defined name explicitly referenced is uniquely referenced when no other name of its disjoint set has the identical spelling and hyphenation (lowercase equivalent to uppercase, §1985:IV.4.2.2.1), so such a name must resolve unqualified, distinct hyphenations (A-B vs AB) must be distinct names, and an identically spelled name that no qualifier distinguishes must be refused; for index-names, which 1985 does not let be qualified (§1985:X.1.3.8.3) and requires to be unique words (§1985:VI.5.8.3 SR14), a duplicate is refused at 85.

edition-consulted.switches: Edition.DialectLevel < 2002: a second INDEXED BY declaration of one spelling is refused (COBOL6863, §1985:VI.5.8.3 SR14); from 2002 duplicates are legal and only an ambiguous reference is refused
ConstructRegistry.Check(Constructs.QualifiedIndexName2002): a qualified index-name reference is refused at 85 (COBOL0900)
only Edition.Permissive (not the edition): the ambiguity verdict for data, index and key names is the same at 85 and 2023

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: for index-names, 85 refuses the duplicate declaration (COBOL6863) and any qualified index-name (COBOL0900); 2023 accepts duplicates and IX OF EA (prints 05). Data-names and condition-names resolve the same way at both.

reader.notes: Unique spellings resolve unqualified with case equivalence and hyphenation significant; identical spellings without distinguishing qualifiers are refused for data-, condition-, index- and paragraph-names. The 85 arms for index-names (unique word, no qualification) are present and fire at --std 85 only.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85, all compile-only refusals with COBOL2692 for one spelling in two disjoint sets: r4a index-name IX and data-name IX; r4b condition-name FOO and data-name FOO; r4c file-name F and data-name F; r4d alphabet-name AL and data-name AL; r4e section-name S1 and paragraph-name S1; r4f program-name R4F and data-name R4F; r4g mnemonic-name CONS and data-name CONS. Nested programs: r4n (EXIT 0) prints INN / OUT / GY / IZ / OUT: the contained program's local X wins over the containing program's GLOBAL G.X, X OF G reaches the global, an outer-only global Y resolves, a local Z hides the outer non-global Z, and the outer program's X is its own; r4h (EXIT 0) prints INNER 04 / OUTER 11: an index-name IX declared in a GLOBAL table and again in a contained program is not refused by the 85 SR14 screen (it walks Forest.IndexNames.Own, per program) and each program resolves its own IX. Checks: 'OK §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.1 ... the text is in the clause'; 'OK §1985:X.1.3.8.2 ... it lies in GR3a'; 'OK §1985:X.1.3.8.3 ... the text is in the clause'; 'OK §1985:VI.5.8.3 SR14 ... the text is in SR14'.
